content.user_title: Improve TypeScript, React, and API Code
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent code quality guidance across TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Node.js, and APIs. This skill provides clear standards, review prompts, and practical examples for maintainable code.
actual_capabilities: Defines readability, simplicity, reuse, and just-in-time design principles.
Gives naming, immutability, async, and type safety guidance for TypeScript and JavaScript.
Covers React component props, custom hooks, state updates, and conditional rendering patterns.
Describes REST endpoint conventions, response shape guidance, and input validation practices.
Includes guidance for file organization, comments, JSDoc, performance, tests, and code smells.
limitations: It does not run linters, tests, formatters, or static analysis tools.
It focuses mainly on TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Node.js, and API projects.
Project-specific rules still need team review and adaptation.
Examples are illustrative and may need changes for each framework or codebase.

use_cases.title: Review pull requests
use_cases.description: Check changed code for naming, type safety, immutability, error handling, and readable structure.

use_cases.title: Create team standards
use_cases.description: Turn broad quality principles into a shared checklist for frontend, backend, and API work.

use_cases.title: Guide AI coding sessions
use_cases.description: Ask an AI assistant to apply consistent patterns while editing TypeScript, React, or Node.js code.
use_cases.target_user: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users

prompt_templates.title: Review code quality basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small file or function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript or JavaScript code against the coding standards. Focus on naming, readability, immutability, types, and simple structure. List the highest priority fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a React component
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate refactor of a component or hook.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component for prop typing, state updates, custom hook usage, conditional rendering, and maintainability. Suggest focused changes without changing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Check API design
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an endpoint or API contract.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API endpoint design for REST conventions, response consistency, input validation, error handling, and pagination. Explain which changes improve reliability.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a feature implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature against the full coding standards. Cover architecture, file organization, performance, tests, documentation, and code smells. Separate required fixes from optional improvements.

output_examples.input: A React component uses untyped props and updates state from stale values.
output: Add explicit prop types so callers receive useful errors.
Use functional state updates when the next value depends on the previous value.
Keep rendering branches simple and avoid deeply nested conditions.

output_examples.input: An API endpoint returns different response shapes for success and failure.
output_examples.output: The review recommends one response envelope, clear error messages, status-specific responses, and validation before business logic runs.

output_examples.input: A feature contains a long function that validates, transforms, and saves data.
output_examples.output: The review suggests splitting validation, transformation, and persistence into named helpers, then adding tests for each behavior.

best_practices: Provide the code, framework, and project constraints before asking for review.
Ask for prioritized findings when reviewing large changes or multiple files.
Validate suggested refactors with tests, type checks, and team conventions.
anti_patterns: Treating every example as mandatory architecture for every project.
Requesting broad rewrites without explaining behavior that must remain stable.
Skipping tests, type checks, and review after applying suggested changes.

faq.question: Does this skill run code?
faq.answer: No. It provides standards, examples, and review guidance for AI-assisted coding work.

faq.question: Which languages and frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Node.js, REST APIs, and common project structure.

faq.question: Can it replace a linter?
faq.answer: No. Use it with linters, formatters, type checks, tests, and human review.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for AI coding assistants and human reviewers.

faq.question: How should I use it during code review?
faq.answer: Paste the relevant code and ask for issues grouped by severity, behavior risk, and maintainability impact.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: It includes input validation and error handling guidance, but it is not a complete security audit framework.
